verdicts.decisive_quote: The target baseline for the monthly copper-price return in November 2025 is unavailable due to the absence of the required historical FRED series data (PCOPPUSDM).
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Best-stated limits in the set (no baseline, magnitude 'insufficient', so centre at base rate and take the middle bucket), but it dismisses the weak-China path as 'contradicted by current evidence' when its own E1 bank carries the 30 October items on China's deepening factory slump, and it labels 'above recent range' compatibility 'unsupported' while handing it 0.40.

ranking_rationale: Both banks are title-only snippets with no numbers, so the separating question was whether a trace kept its confidence inside what direction-only evidence can license: structure_memory, principle_memory, factor_memory and hgf all mapped bullish-but-capped signals onto the middle bucket and said out loud that no magnitude was available. The bottom two took the same qualitative headlines and asserted a move past the 4.016% top-quartile boundary at 0.70 and 0.65 confidence, with case_memory inventing a 4.2% central estimate it called 'evidence-based' one sentence after conceding explicit arithmetic was absent.
shared_evidence_note: The disagreement is almost entirely reasoning, not evidence: E0 and E1 carry the same bullish copper headlines (record highs, rate-cut boost, upward drift despite surplus) and neither contains a single quantity, so the split between 'within' and 'above' came from how far each trace was willing to push direction into magnitude; the one genuine bank difference, E1's China PMI-contraction items, was available only to factor_memory and hgf and neither weighted it (hgf actively waved it away).
